purpose: Define the first controlled comparative matrix for identifying structural similarities and differences across heterogeneous spiritual, philosophical and literary sources without collapsing source-specific meaning.
coding_rules: Use source-native description before abstract labels.
An empty field means not established, not that the phenomenon is absent.
A similarity requires a stated structural reason.
Chronological proximity must not be treated as causal influence without evidence.
A modern Gnozis term may be used only as an analysis label and must not be attributed to the source.
Contradictory structures must remain visible rather than averaged away.
Each cross-source relation carries confidence and provenance.
Interpretive convergence and historical influence are separate relation types.

controlled_corpus_strategy.rule: Start with a deliberately heterogeneous pilot corpus before expanding.
controlled_corpus_strategy.minimum_pilot: At least 5 source families with materially different origins; exact selection is a research decision recorded with provenance.

required: repeated extraction by more than one analytical pass when practical
anti_overfitting.failure_condition: If a pattern appears only after broad abstraction and disappears when source-specific context is restored, classify it as abstraction-induced similarity.

migration_gate: No matrix pattern becomes an engineering requirement without PHIL-004 invariant extraction and PHIL-005 adversarial counterexample analysis.
